sources.citation: Blench, Roger. Ninzic languages: wordlists & papers (index page, rogerblench.info, last edited 19 Oct 2011)
sources.note: Index only; for Anib it lists a single item, 'Unpublished - Anib wordlist' (the PDF above). No other Anib/Kanufi document exists on the site (confirmed by a Wayback CDX listing of the Ninzic directory, 2012-2026).

sources.note: The only substantive hits are mirrors of the same Blench Anib wordlist (rogerblench.info, academia.edu/2776002, scribd 81919121) plus Wikipedia/Ethnologue/Wikidata-derived stubs; no thesis, article or grammar on Kanufi surfaced. Academia.edu copy returned 403 and was not opened.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2006 [printout 19 Oct 2011]. The Anib [=Kanufi] language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment, 25 pp. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. (= Glottolog ref 61329, hhtype wordlist)
sources.note: Nothing. Section 3 'Phonology' (printed pp. 1-2, PDF pp. 3-4) has 3.1 Vowels (eight vowels), 3.2 Consonants (table, final plosive voicing note) and a heading '3.3 Tones' whose body is empty; the words stress/accent/pitch/tonal do not occur anywhere in the text layer. Wordlist entries carry tone diacritics (e.g. Ákpúrkpòd, àrìŋkɔn, únhwɛ́) but no statement about the tone or stress system is made. The 20250524 Wayback capture of the same URL is byte-identical, so no later revision exists on the author's site.
Stub: 'a Plateau language of Nigeria', Kaduna State, c. 10,400 speakers (2000), Ninzic; cites only Ethnologue 18 and Glottolog. Nothing on phonology.
